title: U.S. House · Michigan's 11th District
area: Oakland County, including Southfield, Troy, Farmington Hills and surrounding suburbs.

context.text: This is an open seat with no incumbent on the ballot. Democratic state Sen. Jeremy Moss and Republican former Troy Mayor Ethan Baker advanced from contested primaries.

candidates.name: Jeremy Moss
candidates.currentRole: Michigan State Senator, District 7 (not seeking re-election to that seat)

summary.text: Jeremy Moss is the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 11th District and a Michigan state senator from Southfield. A former Southfield city councilmember and state representative, he has served in the Legislature since 2015, including as Senate President Pro Tem. He is running on healthcare costs, the cost of living and opposition to Trump administration immigration enforcement.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a lifelong Oakland County resident and a graduate of Groves High School; he lives in Southfield.

Earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from Michigan State University. His campaign website says he took part in student humanitarian missions there and then worked under then-Southfield Mayor Brenda Lawrence.
Elected to the Southfield City Council in 2011; his campaign website says he was its youngest-ever member.
Elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (District 35) in 2014 and served from 2015 to 2019.
Won the Michigan Senate seat for District 11 in 2018 and was elected in 2022 to represent District 7, a term that ends in January 2027. He is not seeking re-election to that seat.
In the Senate, chairs the Elections Committee and the Senate Regulatory Reform Committee (2025-2026); earlier terms included chairing the Elections and Ethics Committee.

His campaign website says he led the 2022 effort to win a Democratic Michigan Senate majority and served as Senate President Pro Tem, and that he sponsored the most bills signed into law among state legislators in 2023.
Won the Democratic primary for Michigan's 11th District on August 4, 2026.

priorities.text: Lowering healthcare costs and restoring federal Medicaid and SNAP funding.
priorities.quote: In the State Senate, I protected Michigan from the harshest cuts by restoring funding to Medicaid and SNAP, and enshrined Obamacare in state law when it was under attack in Washington... I strongly support a robust public option as a pathway to universal coverage.

priorities.text: Addressing the cost of living, including housing, tariffs and corporate price gouging.
priorities.quote: We are facing an affordability crisis, from groceries and gas to healthcare and childcare... Congress must overturn the devastating impacts of Trump's big awful bill that have increased costs on Michigan families.

priorities.text: Overhauling federal immigration enforcement while securing the border.
priorities.quote: The cruelty and chaos caused by ICE cannot be repaired or reformed under Donald Trump and the agency must be dismantled... We can both secure our border without allowing officers posing as masked vigilantes to erode due process and civil liberties.

positions.summary: Supports a robust public option as a pathway to universal healthcare coverage.
positions.quote: I strongly support a robust public option as a pathway to universal coverage.

positions.summary: Opposes the Trump administration's tariff policy, saying it has raised consumer prices.
positions.quote: Stopping the chaotic tariff policy: Michigan's economy depends on stable supply chains and strong international partnerships. A tariff policy that changes by the month has only raised prices for consumers and hurt workers and small businesses.

positions.summary: Says ICE should be dismantled and reformed, and supports legal pathways to citizenship for DACA recipients and long-term undocumented residents, while saying the border should still be secured.
positions.quote: We must create legal pathways to citizenship for those protected under DACA and for undocumented immigrants with long-standing ties to the US.

positions.summary: Supports expanding access to pre-K and Head Start programs.
positions.quote: Investing in pre-K and headstart programs: Families should not have to choose between paying the bills and caring for their children. Expanding access to pre-K and Head Start programs would give every child a strong foundation for success.

positions.summary: Cosponsored and voted yes on SB 76 (requiring a license or background check to purchase a firearm), which passed the Michigan Senate 20-17 on 2023-03-16.
Voted yes on SB 8 (raising Michigan's minimum wage to $15 by 2027 and phasing in a higher tipped minimum wage), which passed the Michigan Senate 20-12 on 2025-02-13.

record.text: Chairs the Michigan Senate Elections Committee and the Senate Regulatory Reform Committee for the 2025-2026 session; also serves on the Economic and Small Business Development and Local Government committees.
Cosponsored and voted yes on SB 76 (requiring a license or background check to purchase a firearm), which passed the Michigan Senate 20-17 on 2023-03-16.
Voted yes on SB 8 (raising Michigan's minimum wage to $15 by 2027 and phasing in a higher tipped minimum wage for restaurant workers), which passed the Michigan Senate 20-12 on 2025-02-13.

candidates.name: Ethan Baker

summary.text: Ethan Baker is the Republican nominee for Michigan's 11th District and the mayor of Troy. An attorney who owns a Troy law practice, he worked early in his career for former President Ronald Reagan's post-presidential office. He is running on a message of bipartisan tone and reducing political division.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was raised by a single mother in California and moved to Oakland County with his wife, Bethany, about 17 years ago; they have three children.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Southern California, a law degree from Whittier College School of Law, a Master of Public Affairs from the University of Michigan's Ford School of Public Policy, and a certificate for senior executives in state and local government from Harvard's Kennedy School.
Began as an intern in the post-presidential office of Ronald and Nancy Reagan at age 20 and was then hired, serving more than four years as special assistant, according to his campaign website.
Practices law and owns a law practice in Troy focused on elder law, estate planning, business law and real estate.

Ran unsuccessfully in the 2014 Republican primary for Michigan State Senate District 13 (6.4% of the vote) and the 2018 Republican primary for Michigan House District 41 (44.1% to Doug Tietz's 47.7%).
Elected to the Troy City Council in 2015 and mayor of Troy in 2019; his campaign website says he was re-elected unchallenged and has served as mayor for seven years.
Chairs the Great Lakes Fishery Commission and serves as a U.S. Commissioner; his campaign website describes work restoring U.S.-Canada cooperation on Great Lakes stewardship.

Other civic roles include vice chair of Troy's Downtown Development Authority, chair of the Global Troy Advisory Committee, service on the Local Development Finance Authority, and a seat on the U.S. Conference of Mayors advisory board.
Won the Republican primary for Michigan's 11th District on August 4, 2026.

priorities.text: Says he is running to reduce political division and bring a more respectful, solutions-focused tone to Congress.
priorities.quote: The issues we're facing—cost of living, economic uncertainty, local jobs, infrastructure, our mental and physical health, and safety at home and abroad—need to be addressed now and are too important to be handled through division alone.

record.text: Served as Mayor of Troy, Michigan.
Served as chair and U.S. Commissioner for the Great Lakes Fishery Commission.

candidates.researchNotes: Baker's campaign website statement quoted by Ballotpedia focuses on tone and bipartisanship rather than specific policy positions; no statements matching the guide's fixed issue list were found. Baker's Troy mayoral and Great Lakes roles are as described on his campaign website and Ballotpedia; no independent news profile was reviewed.

candidates.name: Ryan Teasdale

summary.text: Ryan Teasdale is the Green Party candidate on the November ballot for Michigan's 11th District. A nonprofit professional who left a corporate career, he describes his campaign as centered on disagreeing more respectfully, affordable housing, transparency and public safety.

background.text: Graduated from Waterford Mott High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Oakland University in 2009.
Career experience includes working as a nonprofit professional.

In his Ballotpedia survey, says he left a corporate career last year and started a group that demonstrates the benefits of disagreeing more respectfully; the Green Party nominated him at its April 25, 2026 convention.

candidates.researchNotes: Biography draws on Ballotpedia and his self-written survey; no campaign website or news profile was found.

candidates.name: Farid Ishac

summary.text: Farid Ishac is the Libertarian Party candidate on the November ballot for Michigan's 11th District. An automotive engineer, he describes himself as a Wayne State University alumnus running to show voters other choices.

background.text: Born in Livonia, Michigan; graduated from Detroit Catholic Central High School and earned degrees from Wayne State University, according to Ballotpedia.
Career experience includes working as an engineer; in a 2024 Ballotpedia survey he described himself as an automotive engineer with 37 years of experience and a Wayne State MBA.
Nominated at the Libertarian Party convention on June 28, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: Biography draws on Ballotpedia and a 2024 candidate survey; no campaign website or news profile was found.

candidates.name: Anil Kumar

summary.text: Anil Kumar is a physician and member of the Wayne State University Board of Governors running as an independent for Michigan's 11th District. He previously ran as the Democratic candidate for this seat in 2016. He lists get money out of politics, Medicare for All and infrastructure among his priorities.

background.text: Earned an M.D. from Wayne State University; career experience includes working as a medical doctor.
In his Ballotpedia survey, describes himself as a physician, educator and small business owner with more than 30 years serving Michigan families.
Ran in the 2014 Democratic primary for Michigan's 11th District, receiving 31.8% against Bobby McKenzie, and was the Democratic nominee in 2016, losing to Rep. David Trott.
Elected to the Wayne State University Board of Governors in 2018 and took office January 1, 2019; his term ends December 31, 2026 and he is not seeking re-election.
Is on the November ballot as an independent and did not appear on the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary ballot.
